Subject: Questions on liability + termination credits (Order Form #NXT-812)

Diego —

Thanks for the call today. Before we send the Order Form into procurement I need to confirm how Redwood intends to treat (i) limitation of liability (LoL) when a customer terminates for convenience, and (ii) refund mechanics for prepaid fees and any wind-down assistance. A few items we need clarity on so our legal/procurement folks can sign off: 

- Does the liability cap in the MSA apply to refunds of prepaid subscription fees when the customer terminates for convenience? If so, how is the refundable amount calculated and is it subject to mitigation or offsets?
- Is wind-down assistance (knowledge transfer, data export, migration support) treated as a separately billable service post-termination or included in a refund calculation? Do you anticipate charging for up to X days of assistance?
- Are certain categories carved out from the LoL (e.g., gross negligence, willful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, indemnity payments)?

We'd appreciate a redline or sample clause that: (a) shows the refund mechanics (pro-rata vs. prepaid re-allocation), (b) clarifies whether refunds are excluded from the LoL cap or included, and (c) proposes a predictable approach to charging for wind-down assistance so procurement can model costs.

Attaching the current Order Form (v3) for reference.

--
Emily Grant
Senior Counsel, NextRetail Inc.

Emily —

Thanks for the note and clear list. Looping in Marissa (Sales lead on this account) and Lauren (our commercial counsel) to provide the redlines and the legal rationale.

Quick answer so you have expectations: we typically treat prepaid fees as eligible for a pro-rata refund when the customer terminates for convenience, but there are two caveats we want to be transparent about: (1) we apply reasonable mitigation and may deduct costs for agreed wind-down assistance, and (2) large refunds are usually governed by a liability cap approach in the MSA — we can propose language that keeps refunds outside the cap but limits exposure by building in mitigation and short wind-down fee caps.

I've attached our latest MSA redline for context. Marissa / Lauren — can you please prepare (i) a short redline snippet we can send to procurement, (ii) a one-paragraph commercial playbook (what we offer vs walk-away), and (iii) an estimate template for wind-down assistance so they can budget?

Emily / team —

Appreciate the clear ask. Below is our suggested commercial approach and a couple of redline snippets you can consider. High-level playbook first:

- Default position: refunds for termination for convenience = pro-rata refund of prepaid subscription fees for unused period, subject to mitigation (we offset savings and any non-refundable third-party costs).
- Wind-down assistance: we offer up to 30 days of basic handover (data export, runbook delivery) included for free for customers on enterprise commitments; otherwise, chargeable at our standard professional services rate (or a fixed capped fee if the customer requests expedited assistance).
- Liability cap interaction: preferred outcome is to keep refunds of prepaid fees outside the LoL cap, but only if wind-down assistance fees are explicitly deductible and mitigation obligations are codified. If customer insists that refunds fall under the general cap, offer a reduced cap (e.g., 3x monthly recurring fee or $500k floor) in exchange for limiting wind-down assistance obligations.

Proposed clause snippets (for negotiation; legal to formalize):

"Refunds upon Termination for Convenience. If Customer terminates an Order Form for convenience, Redwood will refund Customer on a pro-rata basis for prepaid, unused subscription fees for the remainder of the then-current Term, subject to Customer's reasonable cooperation and Redwood's right to deduct documented wind-down fees and third-party costs incurred in facilitating the transition.

Wind-Down Assistance. Redwood will provide up to thirty (30) days of reasonable wind-down assistance following a valid termination for convenience at no additional charge for customers on annual enterprise commitments; otherwise, chargeable at Redwood's standard professional services rate (or a fixed capped fee if the customer requests expedited assistance).

Interaction with Limitation of Liability. Notwithstanding any other provision, amounts payable by Redwood as refunds of prepaid subscription fees under this Section shall [be excluded from / not exceed] the limitation of liability set forth in Section X, provided that any deductions for wind-down assistance, mitigation or salvage are permitted."
I'm attaching a short text file with the snippets and a simple estimator you can use. Happy to jump on a short call with procurement next week if that helps move things forward.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Emily / Diego / Marissa —

Thanks — I reviewed the redline and Marissa's commercial approach. Below is legal guidance and a recommended redline that balances predictable commercial outcomes with principled risk allocation. Please note I am using section references generically (we will map to the final MSA numbering).

Key legal positions and rationale:
1) Refunds as contract damages vs. contractual credits: Refunds of prepaid fees triggered by termination for convenience are best characterized as contractual remedies rather than 'liquidated damages'. Treating refunds as amounts payable under the Order Form (i.e., direct contract amounts) allows us to narrowly exclude them from a general LoL cap if desired, but only with clear mitigation (deduction) mechanics to prevent double recovery.

2) Exclusions from LoL: Typical carve-outs we support staying out of the LoL include (i) amounts payable in connection with confidentiality breaches, (ii) indemnity payments for third-party claims, and (iii) refunds of prepaid fees for unused services — but only if the clause expressly permits deductions for wind-down assistance and salvage. If we exclude refunds entirely, we should also limit the universe of recoverable refunds to documented prepaid fees net of mitigation.

3) Wind-down assistance: From a legal perspective, it is safer to treat wind-down assistance as a separately identifiable deliverable with a defined scope and cap. Suggested approach: provide limited, defined assistance (up to 30 days) included for enterprise customers; for others, allow Redwood to charge at stated professional services rates or a capped flat fee. This gives procurement certainty while containing our operational exposure.

Recommended redline language (for insertion into Section X and the applicable Order Form):

"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the limitation of liability in Section X shall not limit or exclude (i) amounts payable by a party arising from its breach of confidentiality obligations, (ii) indemnity payments for third-party claims, and (iii) refunds of prepaid subscription fees for the unused portion of the then-current Term following a termination for convenience by Customer, provided that any such refunds shall be reduced by: (A) documented third-party costs reasonably incurred by Provider in winding down Services, and (B) Provider's reasonable costs for providing wind-down assistance, which shall not exceed the cap set forth in the applicable Order Form.

Wind-Down Assistance. Provider shall make commercially reasonable efforts to provide up to thirty (30) days of wind-down assistance following a termination for convenience. For Customers with an annual enterprise commitment, Provider will provide such assistance at no additional charge. For other Customers, Provider may charge for wind-down assistance at Provider's standard Professional Services rates or at a capped flat fee set forth in the Order Form.

Calculation and Payment. Any refund due under this Section will be calculated on a pro-rata basis for prepaid subscription fees for the unused portion of the then-current Term, net of deductions permitted under this Section, and paid within thirty (30) days after Provider's invoice for the refunded amount."

Next steps: if Diego and Marissa are comfortable with the language, I recommend sending the redline to Emily with a brief commercial note (we exclude refunds from the LoL but preserve our right to deduct wind-down fees + cap assistance). If NextRetail pushes back on exclusion entirely, consider the trade: include refunds inside the LoL but agree a concession on reduced cap (example: cap = higher of 3x monthly fees or $750k for the Order Form).

Please confirm and I will prepare a formal tracked-change redline to send to NextRetail legal.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
